## 1. Executive summary

ChainGuard is a controlled local MCP stdio security testbed. It separates deterministic behavioral findings, host authorization/dispatch, independent observation, signed evidence inspection, and fresh complete-run acceptance. M1–M5 and bounded M6 live engineering capabilities exist. This is not a production gateway, universal MCP defense, or completed comparative research study.

**Submission verdict:** a bounded engineering demonstration and accurately qualified project report can be prepared after the licence and packaging gates below. The complete Architecture v1.1 final research study is not finished. No E01–E13 experiment currently has a fully contract-qualified research result. Do not erase these obligations or quietly call them completed to meet closure. The owner must settle the immediate submission wording against the required rubric; this audit does not request a new development sprint.

Key findings:

- All **5,178 existing files and 933 directories** were enumerated, read and SHA-256 hashed without a read failure. This includes hidden Git/environment files; root itself is not counted as a directory. Exactly 711 files are outside .git/.venv: 647 tracked, two untracked SQLite files, and 62 ignored Python caches. The audit document is an additional, post-inventory file.
- **711 project-file purposes are confirmed at role/format level**, with limits stated in the appendix. **4,467 infrastructure-file individual purposes remain unreviewed/uncertain** beyond their Git/environment role, names, sizes and hashes. Reading bytes or identifying a format does not mean every algorithm or record is independently validated. The appendix explicitly separates these levels.
- Both databases must remain outside Git/public handoff: root audit.sqlite is M3 unsealed audit history (52 records, two sessions); the live_m6_current acceptance registry is trusted assessor state (one ACCEPTED run and one session). They are not interchangeable. Neither is currently ignored by the repository's .gitignore.
- The existing comprehensive M1–M5 command source is [SPIKE_LOG.md](SPIKE_LOG.md#historical-engineering-readme-at-checkpoint-5d00057). M6 capture, inspection and acceptance commands are distributed through retained scripts/run metadata. There is no single current professor-ready end-to-end M6 runbook.
- Nine qualified M6 application-source hashes still match the retained owner-pin snapshot. Historical evidence is valuable; no rerun was necessary to establish that byte equality.
- Root LICENSE and the GitHub copy contain only **MIT LICENSE**, without the actual grant, notice or disclaimer. Licence finalization is a hard pre-package gate. The retained E08 upstream MIT licence is separate and complete.
- The current sprint manifest matches **282/283** listed files; its completion-tracker hash is now historical. The older preserved manifest matches **278/282**. Neither is the future distribution manifest.
- Only 62 project Python bytecode caches qualify as SAFE TO REMOVE, subject to individual-path approval. No evidence/database/historical report is approved for removal or movement. There are 57 exact-byte duplicate groups outside caches, but no exact-byte duplicate Markdown documents; identical bytes do not eliminate run provenance.

## 2. Scope, method and limits

Read the charter, Architecture Lock, threat model and playbook; inventoried every directory including empty directories; read/hash all files; inspected project text, JSON structures, raw frame types, source symbols/imports/CLI arguments, reports, logs and reference licences. Parsed all 240 project JSON files successfully; inspected representative records of larger packages/journals rather than dumping them. Checked local Markdown file-link targets (zero missing targets; heading-anchor semantics were not exhaustively checked). Inspected both SQLite databases with Node's DatabaseSync opened with readOnly:true, SELECT and schema PRAGMAs only. Examined schema, primary/foreign keys, row counts and representative records. No application module was imported or executed.

No Git command was run. Read-only parsing of .git/HEAD, the v2 index, loose commit/tree/blob objects and config established working state. Compared index and HEAD, and working bytes with index blobs, explicitly accounting for CRLF/LF. Read 30 reachable commits for author names. This is a direct file assessment, not a claim to have executed git status or every Git filter. No repository-specific attributes file was found.

A shell attempt to use python failed because it is absent from PATH; an attempt to use the existing .venv launcher for a read-only inventory script failed with Access is denied before Python started. No repair, escalation, package installation, test or experiment followed. Node provided the read-only inspection. sqlite3 was not found on PATH. DB Browser installation was not established. The five PDFs are readable one-page PDF 1.4 figure assets, inspected with pdfinfo and their editable SVG companions; PDF raster appearance and final paper compilation were not verified. No DOCX, XLSX, CSV, YAML, standalone SQL, raster image, compiled full-paper PDF, or final distribution archive exists among project files.

GitHub connector confirmed the public repository/owner/main branch and fetched the root and upstream licences. Its normalized metadata omitted the licence identifier. Public page showed a generic License link, not a verified SPDX value; direct licence API retrieval failed. Therefore GitHub's exact detected licence identifier remains **unverified**, not assumed MIT or NOASSERTION. Remote full-tree synchronization was not audited. External legal/distribution policy is not derivable from filenames or repository authorship.

This document is the only authorized new file. All existing files, evidence, databases, configuration and scripts are preserved. The audit does not certify every payload as safe for publication or establish cryptographic validity by hashing alone.

## 5. Actual implementation map

| Component → source | Important function/class | Inputs → outputs | Dependencies and boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1 → client.py / proxy.py / controlled_server.py | exercise; run; call_tool | scripted discovery/list/calls → correlated success/error/success | MCP SDK, stdio; protocol relay alone has no behavioral policy |
| Facts → semantics.py | Policy, Scope, Current, extract_current, project_b1, finding | current args/eligible facts → frozen policy features and distinct decision axes | raw UTF-8/one strict base64 layer of registered synthetic canaries; bounded payload/destinations |
| Detectors → detectors.py | b0, b1, B2Reference.evaluate, B2Streaming.observe/evaluate, equivalent | current features + permitted history → findings/support | semantics; shadows never forward or consume actual grants |
| Synthetic replay → m2.py / oracle.py | ReplayLedger, experiment, assess | separately authored fixture journals → replay results/oracle comparisons | tests/m2_fixtures.py; no live effects or durable execution proof |
| Development qualification → workflows.py | validate_contract, qualify, validate_group | contract plus independent observations → separate outcome axes | tests/workflow_fixtures.py; missing observations remain unknown |
| M3 storage → audit.py / m3.py | AuditSession.append_batch, LiveAudit.before/after, read_records, execute_demo | typed draft batch → durable unsealed rows/receipt | canonical.py, SQLite; exact readback/commit precedes forwarding; no cryptographic commitment |
| M4 evidence → evidence.py / m4.py | ChainedAuditSession.seal, configuration, execute_demo | confirmed stream + frozen head + pinned key → signed package | SHA-256, cryptography P-256; configuration invokes git rev-parse HEAD |
| M4 offline → verifier.py | inspect_package, inspect_run, reproduce_findings | package + external inventory/config/key → dimensions | installed trusted code; no tool execution, no acceptance |
| M5 acceptance → acceptance.py / m5.py | AcceptanceRegistry.register/submit, campaign | expected run and complete packages → ACCEPTED/REJECTED/INCOMPLETE | SQLite transaction, exact readback, duplicate history; campaign imports test fixtures |
| Reservation helper → authorization.py | plan_reservation | required exact scopes + active grant snapshot → all-or-nothing selection | pure helper; cannot create live authority |
| Offline M6 profile → permission_evidence.py / permission_profile.py | reconstruct_lifecycle; inspect_permission_package/run | asserted normalized lifecycle/package → structural/lifecycle/reproduction results | distinct synthetic/offline profile; not a second live host |
| Live contract → m6_live_profile.py | TOOL_CONTRACTS, live_configuration, make_live_manifest | host revision assertion and installed source → bound configuration/manifest | seven fixed synthetic tools; no client grant/revoke API |
| Live persistence → m6_live_audit.py | LiveAuditSession.append_batch, _snapshot_for_export | typed M6 phases → confirmed chained storage/snapshot | code-owned schema; storage is not permission authority |
| Live authority → m6_live_authorization.py | LiveAuthorizationTask.grant/revoke/admit_call/take_dispatch/record_outcome | trusted controls and proposal → permit/refusal/outcome state | confirmed audit writes + plan_reservation; no refund after dispatched failure |
| Host → m6_live_runtime.py | M6Host.open_task; HostTask.serve_client/_work/export_live_evidence | host context + sequential MCP frames → controlled effects and evidence | FIFO worker; complete proposal turns; task-local state and child process |
| Witnesses → m6_live_witness.py / m6_controlled_server.py | WitnessWriter.record; call_tool; _send_to_assessor_sink | host/child/loopback sink observations → assessor JSONL | synthetic bytes only; witnesses do not prove truth against dishonest host |
| Live evidence → m6_live_evidence.py / m6_live_seal.py | validate_live_package_structure; _seal_live_snapshot | frozen clean-close snapshot + key → canonical signed package | structural signature encoding is separate from verified signature |
| Live verifier → m6_live_verifier.py | inspect_live_package, inspect_live_run | package + external pins/config/inventory → seven dimensions | lifecycle and findings reproduced; acceptance remains in acceptance.py |

The authoritative live route is M6Host/HostTask → LiveAuthorizationTask → LiveAuditSession → controlled child → separate outcome write. A trusted grant/revoke is admitted by the host, never inferred from MCP metadata. A supported proposal is normalized; B0/B1/B2 findings remain separate from the host's actual authorization. A complete committed dispatch intent consumes selected permissions once; denial consumes none. Ambiguous commit/outcome halts rather than replaying tools or recovering permission authority from SQLite.

B1 counts scoped grants/revocations/uses without ordering: G>U and R=0 establishes permission; G<=U establishes absence; G>U with R>0 is INDETERMINATE under the conservative operating point. B2-R scans the full prefix; B2-S updates active grants/exposure incrementally. B2-S also retains history, seen facts and issued IDs for references/lifecycle: **do not claim constant total memory**. Their agreement is implementation equivalence, not independent correctness.

Evidence flow: canonical typed events → domain-separated SHA-256 chain and trusted running head/count → clean closure and one reconciled snapshot → ECDSA P-256/SHA-256 signature → independent offline dimensions → optional trusted complete-run acceptance transaction. Hashes alone do not authenticate; signatures do not establish detector accuracy, observed truth or trusted time; evidence duplicate rejection does not prevent tool-execution replay.

No alternate implementation is labeled production-ready. M1–M5 are retained milestone paths; offline M6 profile and live M6 have intentionally different contracts. E08's retained upstream rule/label files are reference code, not ChainGuard dispatch authority. Scripts under results/ are experimental/qualification harnesses with fixed outputs, not a stable general-purpose application CLI.

## 6. Database audit and professor inspection

### 6.1 Database inventory

| Exact repository path | Format / actual role | Contents | Package decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| audit.sqlite | SQLite 3; M3 durable **unsealed** local audit | audit_records: 52 rows, two sessions of 26 each; m3-record-v1, M3_DURABLE_UNSEALED_NO_CRYPTOGRAPHIC_COMMITMENT | Untracked, not ignored. **Exclude from Git and handoff.** Retain locally pending owner decision; not a final signed-evidence database |
| results/completion_sprint_2026-11-02/FIVE_HOUR_SPRINT/live_m6_current/acceptance_registry.sqlite | SQLite 3; trusted assessor expectation/duplicate-acceptance state | expected_runs: one ACCEPTED run; accepted_sessions: one commitment | Untracked, not ignored. Prior explicit public-package exclusion still applies. **Exclude from professor package/public handoff**; use recorded JSON readback for presentation |

There are no other .db/.sqlite/.sqlite3 files or SQLite sidecar journals in the inventory. A header scan is recorded in final verification; database roles come from actual schemas and rows, not just names. Neither existing file is required to start a fresh M1/M2 demo; a fresh audit/registry is created by the relevant authorized workflow. A live acceptance operation requires an appropriately initialized registry, not specifically these historical bytes. No production/customer data is established here: both are controlled engineering data. The exact command that originally produced root audit.sqlite is not retained alongside it; its records establish M3 format and two closed non-release sessions, not its entire provenance.

**audit_records columns:** session_id TEXT, seq INTEGER constrained 1..9007199254740991, event_id TEXT, event_type TEXT, call_id nullable TEXT, run_id TEXT, task_id TEXT, monitor_instance_id TEXT, record_bytes BLOB. Primary key (session_id,seq); unique (session_id,event_id); no foreign keys. record_bytes stores canonical JSON bytes; columns provide indexing/correlation. Observed totals: 2 SESSION_START, 2 SESSION_END, 6 CALL_PROPOSAL, 24 DETECTOR_FINDING, 6 DISPATCH_DECISION, 6 DISPATCH_INTENT, 6 TOOL_OUTCOME. audit.py owns M3 read/write and m3.py is its demo harness. The root file has no M4 manifest/commitment/signature tables; no seal may be inferred from its name or CLOSED row.

**expected_runs columns:** run_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY; challenge TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE; inventory_bytes BLOB; inventory_digest TEXT; config_bytes BLOB; pins_bytes BLOB; state TEXT constrained ACTIVE/ACCEPTED/CANCELLED/FAILED. **accepted_sessions columns:** run_id TEXT referencing expected_runs(run_id); session_id TEXT; commitment_bytes BLOB; commitment_digest TEXT; primary key (run_id,session_id). acceptance.py owns schema/admin/read/write; the retained qualification runner preregisters the run and submit_current.py records acceptance. It is deliberately outside the simulated audit attacker boundary. It is not a tool activity log. Actual run ID: M6Q-01-07-run-24ad1c56a25d4142980292b7cafd64f1, state ACCEPTED.

The professor explanation should be: “The audit store records what the monitor committed. The acceptance registry records what the assessor expected and has already accepted. We inspect a signed package separately, then decide whether a complete expected run is fresh. Neither acceptance nor the database row proves benign behavior.”

Open **DB Browser for SQLite**, not Microsoft Access. Use **File → Open Database Read Only** (or the read-only choice associated with Open Database, depending on installed version). Select the exact root audit.sqlite for the M3 example, or the full acceptance-registry path above for the assessor-state example. Do not open the private local database as a deliverable to copy into the professor package.

Use **Database Structure** to inspect table definitions/indexes. Use **Browse Data**, select audit_records or expected_runs/accepted_sessions, and view records. BLOB values are encoded JSON; use CAST in the SQL examples below for readable text. In **Execute SQL**, paste a SELECT and run it; results appear in the results grid. Do not click Write Changes, import data, run schema changes, or accept editing prompts. Close without saving changes. These are documented UI instructions, not a claim that this audit drove an installed GUI. [DB Browser documentation](https://sqlitebrowser.org/) describes its browse/schema/SQL facilities.

### 6.3 Command-line inspection

sqlite3 was **not found on PATH** in this audit. The following are exact commands **if an existing approved sqlite3.exe is available**; replace only its executable path if it is not on PATH. No installation is authorized here. From repository root in PowerShell:

~~~powershell
sqlite3.exe -readonly .\audit.sqlite ".tables"
sqlite3.exe -readonly .\audit.sqlite ".schema audit_records"
sqlite3.exe -readonly -header -column .\audit.sqlite "SELECT session_id,seq,event_type,call_id FROM audit_records ORDER BY session_id,seq LIMIT 12;"
$cgRegistry = '.\results\completion_sprint_2026-11-02\FIVE_HOUR_SPRINT\live_m6_current\acceptance_registry.sqlite'
sqlite3.exe -readonly $cgRegistry ".tables"
sqlite3.exe -readonly $cgRegistry ".schema"
sqlite3.exe -readonly -header -column $cgRegistry "SELECT run_id,state FROM expected_runs;"
~~~

The -readonly option prevents opening a missing path as a new writable database. See the [SQLite CLI manual](https://sqlite.org/cli.html). Do not use application AcceptanceRegistry construction as a substitute for read-only inspection: the application opens a transactional registry for administration/submission.

If the approved Python runtime works in the owner's terminal, its standard sqlite3 library provides an alternative without installing a CLI. This audit's launcher failure means it was not run here:

~~~powershell
@'
from pathlib import Path
import sqlite3
p = Path('audit.sqlite').resolve()
c = sqlite3.connect(p.as_uri() + '?mode=ro', uri=True)
try:
    print(c.execute("SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'").fetchall())
    print(c.execute('SELECT session_id, seq, event_type FROM audit_records ORDER BY session_id, seq LIMIT 12').fetchall())
finally:
    c.close()
'@ | .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -B -
~~~

### 6.4 Read-only SQL using verified names

Run the first three queries against audit.sqlite:

~~~sql
SELECT session_id, COUNT(*) AS records, MIN(seq) AS first_seq, MAX(seq) AS last_seq
FROM audit_records GROUP BY session_id;

SELECT event_type, COUNT(*) AS records
FROM audit_records GROUP BY event_type ORDER BY event_type;

SELECT seq, event_type, call_id, CAST(record_bytes AS TEXT) AS canonical_record
FROM audit_records
WHERE session_id = '292ff2af-73be-4628-98e4-357d069a7e96'
ORDER BY seq LIMIT 12;
~~~

These show two 26-record streams, the event-phase accounting, and the encoded record body. Contiguous numeric ranges alone do not verify cryptographic integrity or observational completeness.

Run these against acceptance_registry.sqlite:

~~~sql
SELECT run_id, state, inventory_digest FROM expected_runs;
SELECT e.run_id, e.state, COUNT(a.session_id) AS accepted_sessions
FROM expected_runs AS e LEFT JOIN accepted_sessions AS a ON a.run_id=e.run_id
GROUP BY e.run_id,e.state;
SELECT session_id, commitment_digest, CAST(commitment_bytes AS TEXT) AS commitment
FROM accepted_sessions;
PRAGMA foreign_key_list(accepted_sessions);
~~~

These show registered/accepted identity, whole-run/session linkage and committed evidence bytes. Reading is nonconsuming. Do not UPDATE state to ACTIVE to simulate freshness or rerun submission on the historical registry. A future professor database must be freshly generated in an authorized disposable demo location and clearly labeled; both existing excluded files remain private local artifacts.

Example path definitions and existing retained workflow commands for **later owner-run rehearsal**, not audit execution:

~~~powershell
$cgDemoDb = Join-Path $env:TEMP ('chainguard-m3-professor-' + [guid]::NewGuid() + '.sqlite')
$taskM4Directory = Join-Path $env:TEMP ('chainguard-m4-review-' + [guid]::NewGuid())
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -B -m chainguard.m4 demo --directory $taskM4Directory
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -B -m chainguard.verifier --package "$taskM4Directory\evidence.json" --expected "$taskM4Directory\expected.json" --config "$taskM4Directory\configuration.json" --public-key "$taskM4Directory\fixture-public.pem" --key-id chainguard-m4-fixture-key

$taskM5Directory = Join-Path $env:TEMP ('chainguard-m5-review-' + [guid]::NewGuid())
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -B -m chainguard.m5 campaign --directory $taskM5Directory
$taskM5Run = (Get-Content "$taskM5Directory\live\expected.json" | ConvertFrom-Json).run_id
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -B -m chainguard.m5 accept --registry "$taskM5Directory\acceptance.sqlite" --run-id $taskM5Run --package "$taskM5Directory\live\evidence.json"
~~~

M4/M5 cannot be called “Git-free portable demos.” Merely excluding .git makes their installed-configuration revision query fail. The user handles all Git operations; do not run those paths on their behalf under the current instruction. For a future package, choose a user-operated repository-backed workflow or a separately approved demonstration adapter; do not silently alter implementation to remove revision binding.

The M6 historical inspection/submission scripts require:

~~~powershell
$env:CHAINGUARD_ASSESSOR_REVISION_PIN = '89dfbf78a953701cad2eb17da03218ff2abec709'
$env:CHAINGUARD_TRUSTED_CODE_REVISION = $env:CHAINGUARD_ASSESSOR_REVISION_PIN
$env:PYTHONPATH = (Resolve-Path '.').Path
~~~

Those values describe the **retained historical run**, not a fresh authority decision or a claim that current HEAD equals that pin. All nine checked application bytes still match the retained snapshot; the commit identity is an owner assertion. Do not change historical trust inputs to make a new run appear current.

## 8. Tests, experiments and research evidence

The unittest suites under tests/ cover mediation, replay, canonicalization, persistence failures, mutation/cryptography, acceptance restart/concurrency, pure reservation, offline permission profiles, live writer/authority/runtime/sealing/verifier and workflow independence. Some tests create subprocesses, databases and keys in temporary locations; therefore even “just run tests” was outside this audit. The results/FIVE_HOUR_SPRINT/test_research_metrics.py suite is separate from tests/ discovery and checks accounting/provenance, not security outcomes. Appendix D lists source test methods and imports; static counts are not executed test results.

Recorded evidence:

- M1–M5 + foundation: 12 + 41 + 40 + 67 + 27 + 29 = 216 passing tests **across separate historical suites**, not a new full-discovery run or independent research sample.

- E06: raw logs show 13 + 2 = 15 passing existing methods. E11: successful retry logs show 9 + 1 + 4 = 14 passing methods; initial launcher exit 101 remains. These are nonadditive engineering checks, not newly qualified research cases.

## 9. Licence audit and proposed correction

**Current issue:** root [LICENSE](../LICENSE) is ten bytes containing only MIT LICENSE. It does not contain a permission grant, copyright holder/year, conditions or warranty disclaimer. README has no finalized licence section. The [GitHub root licence](https://github.com/aryan0206/ChainGuard/blob/main/LICENSE) fetched through the connector matches this placeholder. The generic GitHub License link does not establish recognized MIT metadata; exact SPDX detection could not be retrieved.

**Verified ownership clues:** GitHub owner aryan0206; all 30 reachable local commit author names are Aryan Malik. main.tex credits **Saanvi Bansal and Aryan Malik**, Manipal Institute of Technology, Manipal Academy of Higher Education. Paper authorship and commit authorship do not independently establish copyright ownership. Confirm both contributors' copyright interests, the institution/course policy, any supervisor/employer claims, and whether the paper/figures/data have separate distribution terms. Do not substitute the acronym MIT (institution) for the MIT software licence.

**Recommendation, conditional on owner confirmation:** if the intended public release permits broad reuse, modification and commercial redistribution with attribution, use the complete standard **MIT licence for original ChainGuard software**, with verified holders and year. This matches the apparent placeholder intent and a simple public research-code release; it is not inferred solely from the project name or dependency licences. MIT permits broad reuse with preservation of copyright/licence notices; see [GitHub's MIT summary](https://choosealicense.com/licenses/mit/). If the intended use is professor-only, noncommercial-only, or source-sharing/copyright conditions beyond MIT, do not adopt MIT automatically: owner must decide the distribution policy first. Public GitHub visibility alone is not a substitute for a permission grant; see [GitHub's no-licence guidance](https://choosealicense.com/no-permission/).

The retained upstream [E08 LICENSE](../results/completion_sprint_2026-11-02/FIVE_HOUR_SPRINT/e08_reference/LICENSE) is complete MIT, copyright 2026 Shanshan Wang / University of Shanghai for Science and Technology, matching the pinned upstream file. Preserve it with the copied reference source regardless of ChainGuard's final licence. Do not reattribute it to the students. Do not copy .venv as a shortcut around third-party redistribution obligations.

**After explicit approval only:** replace root LICENSE with the approved complete text; add consistent README licence/ownership/scope references; clarify treatment of paper/figures/evidence if separately licensed; preserve upstream notice. No pyproject/package metadata file exists requiring an invented licence field. User alone commits/pushes. After the user's publication, re-fetch the remote LICENSE and GitHub licence detection to verify the selected identifier and local/remote consistency. This audit changes neither licence nor GitHub metadata.
